text.p: A earthquake measuring 4.9 on the open-ended Richter scale shook Kagoshima Prefecture in southern Japan on Saturday, Tokyo Broadcasting System (TBS) television reported.

The tremor struck at 1:24 p.m. (0424 GMT) in Sendai and Miyanojocho in northern Kagoshima Prefecture on the southern Japanese island of Kyushu, NHK television quoted a Meteorological Agency source as saying.
The quake was likely an aftershock of an earlier earthquake which hit the same region on March 26 and was followed by several earthquakes of lesser intensity, NHK quoted the source as saying.
The earthquake measured 4.9 on the Richter scale and its epicentre was 10 km (seven miles) deep, the Meteorological Agency source said.
There were no reports of any casualties.
